New protocol carrying bmc-owned device lifecycle and setup-progress state for the boot-time device-info overlay

interface.name: deck_device_info_v1
interface.description:
Lightweight compositor-relayed IPC for the device-info overlay. bmc owns the device lifecycle (setup mode, WiFi provisioning) and its recovery policies; this interface mirrors that state to the overlay for display. It carries no control path: everything the user can trigger from these screens is either overlay-local (touch dismiss) or owned by bmc's own policy timers.
Every event is emitted on bind and again on each change, so a late-binding overlay starts from a complete picture. The bind replay carries current conditions; see setup_progress for the one event whose replay is filtered, since a past transition is not a condition.

enum.name: device_state
enum.description: Mirrors bmc's BmcState and selects which flow the overlay runs.

entry.name: wifi_reconfiguration
entry.summary: setup AP re-opened to change WiFi

enum.name: setup_state
enum.description: Mirrors bmc's InitSetupState, with an extra idle entry so the current value is always well-defined for the on-bind replay.

entry.name: wifi_connection_failed
entry.summary: join failed; the AP screen returns

entry.name: unexpected_error
entry.summary: unrecoverable; bmc will recover on its own (reset or reboot)

event.name: device_state
event.description:
Sent on bind with the current state, then on every change (for example entering or leaving WiFi reconfiguration).
boot_flow_delivered marks this session's operational boot sequence as already handed out, so a client binding after one has run does not start it again. It is a property of the feed rather than of any one client: it latches on the first operational state delivered to anyone, and every later event carries it.

arg.name: boot_flow_delivered
arg.summary: nonzero once an operational boot sequence has been delivered this session

event.name: setup_progress
event.description:
Sent on bind with the latest value, then on every transition. The overlay owns how long each resulting screen stays up; bmc emits transitions the moment they happen.
A screen is owed its time only once the overlay has seen the transition. Clients hold the latest value rather than a queue, so two transitions delivered in one dispatch round leave only the second and the first never gets a screen. Real steps are seconds apart, so this costs a screen only where a step fails on the spot.
This is the one event whose on-bind replay is filtered: it describes a transition rather than a current condition, so it carries only the steps a client cannot derive from the other two events — unexpected_error and connecting_to_wifi. The rest replay as idle, so a completed setup does not announce itself twice.

event.name: access_point
event.description: Sent on bind and on change. A non-empty ssid means the setup AP is up; setup_url is the address the overlay shows and encodes as the QR code on the setup-start screen (bmc owns the AP addressing). Both arguments are empty while the AP is down.

arg.name: setup_url
arg.summary: setup URL, e.g. http://192.168.8.1/, empty when inactive
